items.title: RM4bil needed annually to keep rural road projects on track
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) estimates that RM4 billion is needed annually to keep rural road projects nationwide on schedule. The ministry said the estimate was based on existing commitments and funding required to ensure ongoing projects progressed smoothly. As of Sept 1, 415 rural road projects were under way, involving RM1.995 billion, or 94 per cent, of this year's RM2.107 billion allocation.

items.title: Zetrix AI scraps RM130mil MYEG Ventures deal over share price volatility
items.summary: In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Zetrix AI said it terminated the share purchase agreement with Next Lion Ltd following a review of the deal's commercial rationale due to share price volatility affecting the consideration shares. The termination comes after a sharp sell-off in Zetrix AI shares that began on Aug 27, when the counter closed at 59.5 sen, down nearly 10 per cent from 66 sen a day earlier. The stock then plunged 30 sen, or 50.42 per cent, to 29.5 sen on Aug 28, before falling further to 25 sen on Sept 1 — the same day Zetrix AI signed the RM130 million deal with Next Lion.

items.title: King attends first semi final match of Johor Super Crown Polo tournament
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today graced the first semi-final polo match of the Johor Super Crown Polo Tournament (JSCPT) 2026. According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar's official Facebook page, His Majesty was accompanied by the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail. The first semi-final, featuring Temasek and Korea Polo, was held at the Royal Johor Polo Ground, Istana Pasir Pelangi, here this morning.

items.title: Azalina calls for red flags, warning signs at high-risk Desaru beaches
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Pengerang member of Parliament Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has called for coastal areas in Desaru, including Pantai Tanjung Lompat, to be equipped with red flags and warning signs to deter people from swimming in high-risk areas. She said she had proposed the measure to the local authorities, particularly for beaches with strong currents that are unsuitable for swimming. She said visitors might not be aware of the risks, particularly at campsites without clear signs prohibiting swimming.

items.title: Excel Force co-founder Wang returns as substantial shareholder after seven years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Excel Force MSC Bhd co-founder and former managing director Wang Kuen-Chung has returned as a substantial shareholder of the company, seven years after relinquishing that status and stepping down from its helm. Wang acquired 73.31 million Excel Force shares via the open market on Sept 1, followed by another 10 million shares a day later, taking his direct holding to 89.31 million shares, or 14.645 per cent. The shares added to the six million shares he already held, according to Bursa Malaysia filings today.

items.title: HHRG appoints Syed Azman as executive chairman
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HHRG Bhd has appointed Tan Sri Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim as executive chairman effective today. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the manufacturer and trader of biomass material said Syed Azman holds a doctorate in engineering from Universiti Putra Malaysia. "Today, his automotive portfolio includes Weststar Auto, a leading Honda dealership in Malaysia, Weststar Motors, which specialises in imported luxury cars, and Weststar Maxus, a prominent distributor of commercial vehicles nationwide," the company said.

items.title: 2 houses and 9 vehicles destroyed in fire at Durian Tunggal
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Nine vehicles were destroyed after two semi-permanent semi-detached houses caught fire in Kampung Padang Keladi, Durian Tunggal today. Melaka Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Operations Division director Mohd Shahrom Laji said the nine vehicles included two cars, six motorcycles - including one electric motorcycle - and an electric bicycle. "The fire department received an emergency call at 1.16pm before deploying a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and a Compact Fire Rescue Tender (CFRT), with a strength of seven personnel, along with two Rapid Intervention Motorcycle (RIM) units to the scene about a minute later.

items.title: Pulau Redang coral reef damage under scrutiny, Terengganu to engage stakeholders
items.summary: KUALA NERUS: The Terengganu government will hold an engagement session next week with vari9ious quarters, including representatives from the Department of Fisheries Malaysia, tourism operators and researchers, to discuss coral reef damage at Pulau Redang. However, Razali said preliminary information from the Fisheries Department indicated that the extent of coral reef damage at the resort island remained manageable, although ongoing restoration efforts were necessary. He said the damage to coral reefs at Pulau Redang, including in several marine park areas, was attributed to natural factors rather than tourism activities, as alleged by various quarters.

items.title: Malaysian durians could clear China customs in three to four hours under proposed fast-track scheme
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — Malaysian fresh durians could potentially clear customs in China within three to four hours under a proposed fast-track mechanism being explored by Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB), China Henan Aviation Group Co Ltd (CHAG) and Tropika Makmur Manufacturing Sdn Bhd (TMM). According to MAHB in a statement, the proposed “inspect-on-arrival and release-upon-compliance” model under KUL-CGO Smart Durian Fast Track would enable the entire process, from aircraft arrival to document formalities and cargo collection, to take only three to four hours. “The Smart Durian Fast Track will explore improvements spanning handling and inspection, free zone access, customs coordination, permit and certification visibility,” it added.

items.title: Explainer: What the Serian haze emergency means
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A haze emergency is the highest level under Malaysia's Air Pollutant Index (API) classification and applies when the reading exceeds 500. Why was an emergency declared? Under the National Haze Action Plan, a haze emergency may be declared when the API reaches 500 or higher.

items.title: ByteDance secures $29.6 billion loan in AI push, sources say
items.summary: HONG KONG: ByteDance has secured a US$29.6 billion loan from nearly 30 banks, three people with direct knowledge of the matter said on Friday, with the Chinese social media giant's bet on AI development driving strong interest from lenders. Chinese, U.S., European and Singaporean banks are participating in the financing, the people said, with the three-year loan co-ordinated by Citigroup and JPMorgan set to be signed by ByteDance shortly. RARE UNSECURED MEGA LOAN ByteDance has stepped up its AI spending.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 4, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Bursa Malaysia closed lower on Friday dragged by weakness in the plantation sector as investors took profit following the sector's strong recent performance. The index is expected to maintain a positive bias next week, supported by resilient domestic fundamentals and improving regional sentiment. Following the trend, Ethereum traded higher at RM10,163, while Solana stood at RM418.

items.title: Nepal's 'Himalayan tsunami': What we know
items.summary: Here is what experts – including from the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) and the HiRISK group, focusing on Asia's mountains – have deciphered so far. Water and debris then burst downstream. - WHY DID THE MOUNTAIN COLLAPSE?

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia, Macau to strengthen strategic ties and unlock new business opportunities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia and Macau remain committed to strengthening bilateral relations and enhancing strategic cooperation across various fields, including trade and investment, finance, science and technology, education, and the convention and exhibition industry. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that this commitment also encompasses efforts to leverage the strategic positions of Macau and Hengqin, which are connected to the Greater Bay Area (GBA), for Malaysian companies to explore business opportunities. The visit marks Sam’s inaugural trip to Malaysia since assuming office as Macau’s Chief Executive in December 2024.

items.title: RM4.25mil project to ease flash floods in Kampung Pokok Asam
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A RM4.25 million flood mitigation project at Parit Monsun, Kampung Pokok Asam is expected to improve drainage capacity and reduce flash floods. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the project, which began on July 26, 2024, was crucial to addressing flooding in the low-lying area, which frequently experiences excess water during heavy rain. "The project is expected to reduce flash floods that occur several times a year, particularly during heavy rain and high tides.

items.title: MACC drops orange garb requirement for suspects brought to court for remand
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has suspended the use of the orange garb for people under investigation who are brought to court for remand applications, with immediate effect. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the move is in response to recent developments and current recommendations on procedures for handling people under investigation, particularly when they are brought to court. “Individuals under investigation may wear their own clothes when brought to court, while lockup attire will only be required while they are being held in detention,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Man returns to Kelantan for Pas Muktamar, learns cyclist brother killed in crash
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A man who had just returned from Selangor to attend the 72nd Pas Muktamar here was left devastated after learning that his younger brother was among two best friends killed when a car crashed into them while they were cycling today. Private-sector worker Zamri Risman Mahmet, 52, said he received a call from his younger brother and uncle about 10.30am informing him that his 49-year-old brother, Zamrie Rismawadi, had been killed in the accident. Zamri said he last met his brother about two months ago.

items.title: Ringgit ends lower against US dollar as US rate hike debate persists
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit finished lower against the US dollar on Friday as the market closely monitors the ongoing debate regarding interest rate hikes in the United States. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit was fairly stable despite market uncertainties. The ringgit traded mostly lower against regional currencies.

items.title: Haze persists nationwide, Serian remains worst-hit
items.summary: As of 6pm, two of 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, according to the Department of Environment's API Management System. Two locations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy readings – Samarahan (292) and Sri Aman (241). Elsewhere, 37 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality, while 13 recorded good readings.

items.title: Haze threatens ecosystems, wildlife populations
items.summary: Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) Environmental Governance expert Assoc Prof Dr Haliza Abdul Rahman said among the significant impacts on fauna were chronic respiratory damage, decreased reproduction rates, dehydration and lack of food sources. "The haze does not only affect humans, but also animals and plants. Haliza said thick haze also reduced visibility for wildlife, resulting in a higher risk of these animals straying from their natural habitats into forest fringes or human settlements.

items.title: Anwar says orange detention garb unnecessary for those cooperating with investigations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Individuals who fully cooperate with investigations should not have to wear orange detention garb when brought to court before they are formally charged, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. “I said yesterday that before prosecution, or before a person is brought to court and charged, there is no need to wear orange detention garb. On Tuesday, a former minister was brought to court wearing the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) orange detention garb for a remand application in connection with an investigation into a hotel lease involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Nepali foreman rescued after nine days says he stayed behind to save others
items.summary: KATHMANDU: When the mountain gave way above the Nepali power plant where Sanjay Sah worked, he had a choice: flee, or stay. The mechanical foreman was rescued on Friday alongside another worker, nine days after a wall of ice, rock and debris levelled the valley where the Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station was located, providing a rare glimmer of hope in search operations for thousands missing after the unprecedented disaster. Officials believe at least 900 people are trapped in tunnels related to six hydropower projects along the Trishuli river.

items.title: Transboundary haze poses long-term threat to wildlife, disrupting habitats, food sources and reproduction
items.summary: Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) Environmental Governance expert Assoc Prof Haliza Abdul Rahman said among the significant impacts on fauna were chronic respiratory damage, decreased reproduction rates, dehydration and lack of food sources. “The haze does not only affect humans, but also animals and plants. Haliza said thick haze also reduced visibility for wildlife, resulting in a higher risk of these animals straying from their natural habitats into forest fringes or human settlements.

items.title: 647 Sarawak schools to close for 5 days over haze
items.summary: The closures involve 563 primary schools with 108,477 pupils and 84 secondary schools with 90,082 students under 12 district education offices. Sarawak Education director Omar Mahli said the department prioritised the welfare, health and safety of students, particularly amid hot weather and unpredictable conditions. Omar also advised schools to refer to Education Ministry Circular Letter No.

items.title: Nicol David among eight honoured with 2026 Merdeka Award
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Eight Malaysians and organisations whose work spans humanitarian relief, conservation, science, academia and sports have been named recipients of the 2026 Merdeka Award. Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) president and group chief executive officer Tengku Tan Sri Muhammad Taufik said the award embodied the "Spirit of Merdeka" by recognising individuals and organisations whose work had made a difference to Malaysia and improved the lives of Malaysians. [[nid:1525771]] He said the achievements of the Merdeka Award laureates served as a reminder that transformational contributions were not necessarily the work of extraordinary people, but often came from ordinary individuals driven by extraordinary missions.

items.title: Felda cooperative to pay share withdrawals in stages, prioritise critical cases
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Payments for share withdrawal applications by Koperasi Permodalan Felda Malaysia Bhd (KPF) members will be made in stages and on a rotational basis, with priority given to special and critical cases. KPF said these included medical expenses, education, property matters, haj, umrah and other religious needs, subject to sufficient cash flow. "KPF acknowledges that there are still outstanding share withdrawal applications that have yet to be paid.

items.title: MACC suspends orange garbs for remand detainees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has suspended, with immediate effect, the requirement for persons under investigation to wear its orange uniform when brought to court for remand proceedings. The move comes after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said earlier today that political leaders would be given leeway not to wear the MACC orange uniform when brought to court. Earlier today, Anwar said political leaders would be given leeway not to wear the MACC orange uniform when brought to court.

items.title: Police probe possible gang link in Sungai Lembu shooting
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Police are probing the possible involvement of gangs in a shooting that injured a 43-year-old man in Machang Bubok yesterday. Seberang Prai Tengah police chief Assistant Commissioner Nik Aminuddin Raja Abdullah said investigations were ongoing to determine the motive, identify the suspects and establish whether gangs were involved. The victim ran towards the Chinese cemetery to seek safety.

items.title: Sarawak to close 647 schools for five days from Sept 7 to 11 as haze persists
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 4 — A total of 647 schools in Sarawak will be closed for five days from September 7 to 11 due to persistent haze with no significant signs of improvement. Sarawak Education director Omar Mahli said the closure involved 563 primary and 84 secondary schools across several districts, reported Astro Awani. The affected schools are under the Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu, Kanowit, Julau and Maradong district education offices.

items.title: Car hits cyclists, killing two best friends in Kota Baru
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Two cyclists were killed after they were hit by a car at Km18 of the Kota Baru-Ketereh Highway here this morning. They were identified as Zamrie Rismawadi Mahmet and Nik Zaki Yamani Nik Abdul Aziz, both 49. The two best friends were believed to have been cycling with seven friends as part of their routine cycling activity during public holidays.

items.title: King consents to emergency declaration in Serian as haze reaches hazardous levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has approved the declaration of an emergency throughout the Serian Division in Sarawak following worsening haze that has reached levels hazardous to public health and safety. The Prime Minister’s Office said the decision was made after taking into account the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg and relevant agencies on air quality in the affected area. The declaration covers the entire Serian Division in Sarawak.

items.title: Court rejects Maju Holdings director, wife's DNAA bid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sessions Court here today dismissed an application by Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd director Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on charges of criminal breach of trust and money laundering. Judge Suzana Hussin rejected the application after lawyer Jasbeer Singh, representing Abu Sahid, 75, and Puan Sri Noor Azrina Mohd Azmi, 49, made the application during case management proceedings. Earlier, Jasbeer sought a DNAA on the grounds that the prosecution had yet to hand over important documents related to the case, despite the charges being brought a year ago.

items.title: TMJ says no issue paying Singapore tax on land sale exceeding RM4b
items.summary: JOHOR BARU, Sept 4 — Johor Regent Tunku Ismail Sultan Ibrahim says he has no reservations about paying a hefty tax bill linked to the planned sale of his 16.6-hectare landholding in Singapore. The Star reported that Tunku Ismail, who is also the Johor Crown Prince, responded on X to reports of a potential land betterment charge exceeding US$1 billion (RM4.05 billion), saying he had no qualms about paying taxes and contributing to both countries. The planned land sale involves parcels on Holland Road that Tunku Ismail owns following a land-swap agreement with the Singapore government in June 2025.

items.title: [UPDATED] King consents to emergency declaration in Serian [WATCH]
items.summary: At 2pm today, haze in Serian, Sarawak lingered at hazardous levels, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 521. Two locations recorded very unhealthy readings — Samarahan (284) and Sri Aman (235). Meanwhile, 11 locations recorded unhealthy readings: Sarikei (182), Sibu (181), Mukah (177), Bintulu (157), Kota Kinabalu (152), Tawau (151), Samalaju (146), Sandakan (140), Pasir Gudang, Johor (128), Segamat, Johor (115), and Miri (112).

items.title: Anwar tells Rural Development Ministry and MOF to find middle ground in funding row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today called on the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to resolve issues concerning allocations, including delayed payments to contractors, through discussions. On Thursday, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said there were no restrictions on KKDW allocations for rural road projects, with the full allocation for the projects having already been channelled. The issue arose following a statement by Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi regarding problems faced by contractors following delays in payments for projects under his ministry.

items.title: Teen drowns off Pantai Klebang, mother mourns family's hope
items.summary: Mazan, a general assistant at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bukit Rambai, said Arif, the youngest of two siblings, had been the family's hope of caring for his older sister, who has Down syndrome. She said the siblings shared a close bond, with Arif helping to attend to his sister's needs since he was young. "She kept saying, 'Arif, Arif'.

items.title: [UPDATED] Court dismisses challenges to 2021 Parliament suspension during Covid-19 emergency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today dismissed legal challenges by two lawmakers, the Malaysian Bar, Bersih 2.0 and others over the suspension of Parliament during the 2021 Covid-19 emergency. Judge Datuk Aliza Sulaiman ruled that the court could not grant declarations sought to invalidate provisions of the Emergency (Essential Powers) Ordinance 2021, including Section 14, which suspended Parliament. Aliza said Article 150(8) of the Federal Constitution barred the court from ruling on challenges to the validity of an emergency ordinance, including challenges to individual provisions.

items.title: Anwar endorses proposal for SC or BNM oversight of Tabung Haji investments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today backed a proposal by Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to place its investment operations under the regulatory oversight of the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) or Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). He said the initiative by TH’s new management, led by its chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain, was a positive step towards strengthening governance and accountability at the pilgrimage fund management institution. Yesterday, Abdul Rashid said TH was refining a new regulatory framework to place its investment operations under the statutory oversight of the SC.

items.title: WhatsApp engineers guide Nepal tunnel rescue as two workers found alive
items.summary: KATHMANDU: An army of experts in a WhatsApp group is guiding rescue workers scouring a Nepali valley after a huge flash flood more than a week ago as they desperately search for anyone who may be alive inside tunnels of devastated hydropower plants. One of them said there could be more survivors in the tunnels. Nepal's Independent Power Producers' Association said on Monday at least eight people could be trapped at Chilime, while an official at the Nepal Electricity Authority said 46 may be trapped at Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant, further south.

items.title: Eight men charged with murder over fatal Taman Alam Megah brawl
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 4 — Eight men, including two alleged secret society members, were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of a man during a brawl involving a group of individuals in Taman Alam Megah last month. Puwaneswaran, 39; A. Rhubban, 37; K. Thivagar, 29; Shaik Hasanudin Ahlauwudin, 26; Sheikh Mauludin Ahlauwudin, 24; and R. Darvin Raj, 23, nodded after the charge was read out to them before Magistrate Cynthia Noor Haizean Sulaiman. The remaining accused were unrepresented.

items.title: Prosecution to appeal Rosmah ruling allowing additional evidence, says AG
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — The prosecution will appeal the Court of Appeal’s decision allowing Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence for corruption involving the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project. “It merits an appeal to the Federal Court. On Tuesday, a three-man bench of the Court of Appeal comprising Justices Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy allowed Rosmah’s application to submit additional evidence in her appeal against her corruption conviction and sentence.

items.title: Court rules DNAA not applicable in Maju Holdings director, wife’s CBT, money laundering case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — The Sessions Court here has rejected an application for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in the criminal breach of trust (CBT) and money laundering case involving Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd director Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife. Abu Sahid claimed trial to 17 charges involving CBT and money laundering linked to the proposed MEX II Highway project on September 8 last year. He faces four CBT charges involving RM313 million and 13 money laundering charges involving RM139 million, allegedly committed between May 2016 and October 2019.

items.title: BN backs unity govt despite push for earlier GE16, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Barisan Nasional remains committed to the unity government and the country’s political stability despite calls within the coalition for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be held earlier, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir. The Star reported that Zambry said BN’s support for the unity government remained firm, stressing that calls for an earlier election should not be interpreted as confidence that the coalition would automatically regain federal power. He said there was no intention among BN’s partners to undermine or bring down the unity government before the next general election.

items.title: Malaysian man jailed six years in Australia for keeping Indonesian woman as slave
items.summary: MELBOURNE, Sept 4 — A Malaysian man has been sentenced to six years in prison in Australia after being convicted of enslaving and assaulting an Indonesian woman. Free Malaysia Today, citing ABC News, reported that Melbourne County Court Judge Michael Cahill sentenced Chong Chee Kit, 47, after a jury found him guilty of forcing the woman into domestic servitude and subjecting her to repeated abuse. A jury in May found Chong guilty of keeping the woman, who was in her 60s, in slavery between February and October 2022.

items.title: Penang steps up action to curb sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 4 — The Penang state government has taken several measures to address sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat, near Tasek Gelugor, including requiring all farms in the area to send their wastewater to a biogas plant in Ampang Jajar. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H’ng Mooi Lye said the move is part of the state government’s efforts to prevent livestock farm sewage from being discharged directly into drains or rivers in the area. “The matter was discussed at a meeting with the state Veterinary Services Department and the state assemblyman for the area in April, and the state government has required all pig farms in Kampung Selamat to send their sewage waste to the biogas plant in Ampang Jajar since May.

items.title: Anwar to discuss further action on Sarawak haze with Abang Jo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Further action, including the possibility of declaring a disaster emergency following an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeding 500 in Serian, will be discussed with the Sarawak government, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said he had contacted Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg yesterday to discuss the matter. This morning, air quality in Serian, Sarawak, remained at a hazardous level, with the monitoring station at the local District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 518.

items.title: Azalina calls for red flags at Desaru beaches after three teens drown
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — Pengerang Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has called for coastal areas in Desaru, including Pantai Tanjung Lompat, to be equipped with red flags and warning signs to deter people from swimming in high-risk areas. She said she had proposed the measure to the local authorities (PBT), particularly for beaches with strong currents that are unsuitable for swimming. She said visitors might not be aware of the risks, particularly at campsites without clear signs prohibiting swimming.

items.title: Lorry driver remanded three days over crash that killed 12-year-old boy in Gurun
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police have detained a 40-year-old lorry driver over a crash involving a motorcycle on Jalan Gurun-Jeniang yesterday that killed a 12-year-old boy. The victim, Muhammad Ilham Firdaus Mohamad Iruan, 12, died at the scene from severe injuries. Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the suspect was detained to assist investigations into the crash, Harian Metro reported.

items.title: Retired military officer with ‘Datuk’ title charged over alleged caddie molestation in Ayer Keroh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — A 68-year-old retired military officer holding the title “Datuk” was charged in the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court here today with using criminal force with intent to outrage the modesty of a 20-year-old female caddie last month. The charge alleged that Yahya used criminal force against the victim with intent to outrage her modesty at the Tiara Melaka Golf & Country Club golf course in Jalan Gapam, Bukit Katil, in Ayer Keroh, Melaka, between 8.30am and 12.30pm on August 25. The court was also told that Yahya had a prostate-related health condition requiring treatment.

items.title: Perlis police arrest activist over incendiary TikTok on Sri Veera Maha Kaliamman Kovil temple
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 4 — A 55-year-old activist has been remanded for two days from today on suspicion of making an inciting post via social media related to the organisation of a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple here on Aug 22. Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the man, who works as a consultant, was arrested in Petaling Jaya, Selangor yesterday at 10 am. He said that earlier, the Perlis police received 14 reports regarding posts on the activist’s TikTok application between Aug 22 and 27.

items.title: Third missing teenager’s body recovered at Kota Tinggi beach
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — The body of a third missing teenager has been recovered from the waters near Tanjung Siang, following a tragic incident at Tanjung Lompat in Bandar Penawar. The victim, 16-year-old Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal, was found floating by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 11.15am today, approximately five kilometres from the site of the initial incident. Kota Tinggi deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed the discovery.

items.title: MAG says mass drug screenings for Malaysia Airlines crew near 100pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has completed drug screenings for nearly all Malaysia Airlines cabin crew following the arrest of a pilot in Jakarta, president and group chief executive officer Capt. Nasaruddin A. Bakar said today. On Aug 17, MAG announced that all operationally active Malaysia Airlines pilots had undergone drug tests and tested negative.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines resumes Busan flights starting December
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia Airlines will resume flights to Busan, South Korea's second-largest city, starting December this year as the national carrier expands its network and pushes to return to profitability. Malaysian Aviation Group chief executive officer Capt Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the Busan service is one of several new routes the airline group expects to launch, including expansion by its budget unit Firefly, which recently added China's Kunming to its destination network. MORE TO COME

items.title: Two dead in Jasin motorcycle crash after overtaking manoeuvre fails
items.summary: Jasin district police chief Supt Lee Robert said both victims, a 21-year-old college student and a 41-year-old lorry driver, died on the spot in the incident, which occurred at about 11.30 pm. He said initial investigations found that the student was travelling from Bemban towards Ayer Keroh, while the lorry driver was heading in the opposite direction, towards Bemban from Ayer Keroh. Lee said police were unable to obtain any CCTV or dashcam footage of the incident.

items.title: Tahfiz students perform prayers to support search for missing teens in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — For the second consecutive day, students of Madrasah Tahfiz Al-Quran Ar-Redha in Bandar Penawar recited the azan and Yasin and performed Dhuha and hajat prayers as the search continued for two teenagers feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach here. Islamic Education teacher Mohd Azroy Azhar said the students took the initiative voluntarily after seeing the various efforts by the authorities and the victims’ families to locate the missing teenagers. He said the students were also doing their part by offering prayers and supplications, hoping that the two missing teenagers would be found soon.

items.title: PAS sets seven priorities for GE16, including wider political cooperation
items.summary: The New Straits Times reported that PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the party’s Muslim unity agenda would see it continue defending Islam while honouring agreements reached with other parties. “PAS is prepared to cooperate with any party on matters that benefit the country without compromising its policies and principles,” he said. Abdul Hadi was speaking when delivering his policy speech at the opening of PAS’ 72nd Annual Muktamar in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, today.

items.title: Police refer case of man accused of provoking crowd at National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya to DPP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police are awaiting further instructions from the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) after referring an investigation paper on a man accused of causing a disturbance and provoking the crowd during the National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31. Putrajaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said the investigation paper was referred to the DPP’s office yesterday for further action, BuletinTV3 reported. Police had previously reported that a man was detained for allegedly causing a disturbance and provoking members of the public during the National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Monday.

items.title: Serian API hits hazardous 518, emergency declaration possible
items.summary: SERIAN, Sept 4 — Serian recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 518 as of 10 am today, placing it in the “hazardous” category amid transboundary haze. According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), an API reading above 300 is classified as hazardous, while readings between 201 and 300 are categorised as “very unhealthy”. Kuching also recorded a hazardous API reading of 310, followed by Kota Samarahan at 281 and Sri Aman at 245.

items.title: Six held over Malaysian co-pilot’s Jakarta drug case after four fled to Thailand, Vietnam and returned
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Bukit Aman’s Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (JSJN) has detained six local men over a drug smuggling case involving a Malaysian co-pilot arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Tangerang, Banten, Indonesia, with four of the suspects having fled to Thailand and Vietnam after learning of his arrest. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the six were believed to have acted as suppliers and couriers who provided drugs to the co-pilot. Meanwhile, Harian Metro reported that Hussein said two of the suspects had fled to Thailand while another two went to Vietnam after learning of the co-pilot’s arrest.
